# Data Preparation 

Note: 1. Values were added to biomarkers before log-transformation to make it the most normally distributed), and 2. participants on diuretics and lithium were filtered out for analysis due to the medications confounding with AVP secretion. 

```{r load data}
ket <- read_excel("Copeptin_prepostket.xlsx")
ket$Code <- as.factor(ket$Code)
ket$Dx <- as.factor(ket$Dx)
ket$Diuretics <- as.factor(ket$Diuretics)
ket$Lithium <- as.factor(ket$Lithium)

# Create log-transformations; added numbers to raw values to make the log-transformed values most normally distributed
ket <- ket %>%
  mutate(
    Log_Copeptin = log(Copeptin + 2),  # Adding 0.01 to avoid log(0)
    Log_ACTH = log(ACTH + 0.5), 
    Log_CRH = log(CRH + 0.1),
    Copeptin_CRH_Ratio = Log_Copeptin - Log_CRH,
    Copeptin_ACTH_Ratio = Log_Copeptin - Log_ACTH,
    `Subject ID` = Code,
    Time_Min = case_when(
           Timepoint == 1 ~ -60,
           Timepoint == 2 ~ 230,
           Timepoint == 3 ~ 1440  #24 hrs in minutes
         ))

#Create named vector for x-axis labels for Visualization
time_labels <- c("-60 min", "+230 min", "+24 hr")
names(time_labels) <- c(-60, 230, 1440)

# Extract behavioral data
RISC2 <- read_excel("RISC Phase II.xlsx")
RISC2$Code <- as.factor(RISC2$Code)

# Filter out timepoint = 0 (baseline)
ket_filtered <- ket %>%
  filter(Timepoint != 0)

# Create baseline values at timepoint = 1 for each subject
ket_baseline <- ket_filtered %>%
  filter(Timepoint == 1) %>%
  select(Code, Log_Copeptin, Log_CRH, Log_ACTH) %>%
  mutate(Baseline_Copeptin = Log_Copeptin, 
         Baseline_CRH = Log_CRH, 
         Baseline_ACTH = Log_ACTH) %>%
  select(Code, Baseline_Copeptin, Baseline_CRH, Baseline_ACTH) 

# Merge baseline values back into the dataset
combined_ket <- ket_filtered %>%
  left_join(ket_baseline, by = "Code") 

# Merge behavior/symptoms
combined_ket <- combined_ket %>% left_join(RISC2, by = c("Code", "Timepoint"))


```

```{r linear vs. mixed model}
### Small sample size, mixed model or simple regression better fit ? 
mod1 <- lmerTest::lmer(Log_Copeptin ~ Timepoint + (1|`Subject ID`), data = combined_ket)
mod2 <- lm(Log_Copeptin ~ Timepoint, data = combined_ket)
anova(mod1,mod2) 
#lmer model has less AIC, better fit, so will use lmer (mixed model)

```

```{r filter data}

#101 = on lithium and diuretics, but trajectory of copeptin not different from others so include
#109 = on diuretics but spironolactone (weak) for feminization; copeptin trajectory also similar to others so include

  filter(`Subject ID` != 507)
```

```{r linear mixed models, while controlling for baseline}

summary(lmerTest::lmer(Log_Copeptin ~ Timepoint + Baseline_Copeptin + (1|`Subject ID`), data = combined_ket)) 
summary(lmerTest::lmer(Log_CRH ~ Timepoint  + Baseline_CRH + (1|`Subject ID`), data = combined_ket))
summary(lmerTest::lmer(Log_ACTH ~ Timepoint + Baseline_ACTH + (1|`Subject ID`), data =combined_ket))
summary(lmerTest::lmer(Copeptin_CRH_Ratio ~ Timepoint + Baseline_Copeptin + Baseline_CRH + (1|`Subject ID`), data = combined_ket)) 
summary(lmerTest::lmer(Copeptin_ACTH_Ratio ~ Timepoint + Baseline_Copeptin + Baseline_ACTH + (1|`Subject ID`), data = combined_ket)) 

# linear mixed models assuming a linear trajectory across timepoints were not significant fits for all biomarkers, also  consistent with visual inspection of the spaghetti plots
```

```{r linear estimated modeling}

# Load necessary libraries
library(lme4)
library(emmeans)

# Filter to -60min and +230min timepoints
acute_data <- combined_ket %>% 
  filter(Timepoint %in% c(1, 2))

# Create named labels for plotting
time_labels <- c("-60 min", "+230 min")
names(time_labels) <- c(1, 2)

# List of outcome variables
outcomes <- c("Log_Copeptin", "Copeptin_CRH_Ratio", "Copeptin_ACTH_Ratio")
# Loop over each outcome
for (outcome in outcomes) {

  # Base model with baseline copeptin
  base_formula <- paste0(outcome, " ~ Timepoint * Dx + Baseline_Copeptin")

  # Add appropriate baseline covariates
  if (grepl("ACTH", outcome)) {
    base_formula <- paste0(base_formula, " + Baseline_ACTH")
  } else if (grepl("CRH", outcome)) {
    base_formula <- paste0(base_formula, " + Baseline_CRH")
  }

  # Complete model with random intercept
  formula <- as.formula(paste0(base_formula, " + (1 | `Subject ID`)"))

  # Fit the model
  model <- lmer(formula, data = acute_data)

  # Estimated marginal means
  emm <- emmeans(model, ~ Timepoint | Dx)
  emm_df <- as.data.frame(emm)

  # Create a time label factor
  emm_df <- emm_df %>%
    mutate(Time_Factor = factor(Timepoint, levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("-60 min", "+230 min")))

  # Generate plot
  p <- ggplot(emm_df, aes(x = Time_Factor, y = emmean, group = Dx, color = Dx)) +
    geom_line(size = 1) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = emmean - SE, ymax = emmean + SE), width = 0.1) +
    labs(
      title = paste0("Estimated ", outcome, " Change (–60 to +230 min)"),
      x = "Time Relative to Infusion",
      y = "Estimated Marginal Mean ± SE",
      color = "Diagnosis"
    ) +
    scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(
      plot.title   = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 14),
      axis.text    = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
      axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold")
    )

  print(p)
}



```

```{r　change in biomarkers in relation to symptoms}
summary(lmer(CSSRS_IDEATION_SCORE ~ Log_Copeptin * Dx + Time_Min + (1|`Subject ID`), data = combined_ket))
summary(lmer(CSSRS_IDEATION_SCORE ~ Copeptin_CRH_Ratio * Dx + Time_Min + (1|`Subject ID`), data = combined_ket))


# Across four symptom domains, neither the raw copeptin signal nor the copeptin/CRH ratio demonstrated a consistent, statistically reliable relationship with psychiatric outcomes over the ketamine protocol. Interactions with PTSD comorbidity showed small positive coefficients—hinting that the biomarker–symptom link might be subtly stronger in MDE+PTSD—but these effects were imprecise and only slightly improved model fit. Thus, in this sample, acute AVP‐related changes do not appear to drive mood, anxiety, or suicidality trajectories, underscoring the specificity of the physiologic response and its limited immediate behavioral predictive power.
```
